newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's INCA delays launch of rand bonds 2 weeks.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's INCA delays launch of rand bonds 2 weeks.

text.p: South Africa's Infrastructure Finance Corp (INCA), set up last October, said on Tuesday it was delaying the private placement of 500 million rand of bonds for two weeks until February 25.

Originally INCA had scheduled the placement of the 13.5 percent 10-year bonds for February 11, but a spokesman said the date had been put back due to some delays in the prospectus. A local roadshow for the issue commenced last week and will finish on Tuesday.

Further issues of 300 million rand of 13.5 percent 10-year bonds, 200 million rand of 13.5 percent five-year bonds and 200 million rand of 14 percent 15-year bonds will be taken up by First National Bank, one of INCA's main shareholders.
All the bonds are now due to be listed on the Bond Exchange of South Africa on March 7.
INCA, established to help fund infrastructure projects throughout South Africa, announced at the time of its launch that it intended to raise 1.2 billion rand from investors in 1997.
In total, INCA intends to raise 12 billion rand over the next seven years in a process which will see the private sector joining government in addressing the country's massive infrastructure backlog.
Government estimates put South Africa's total infrastruture needs at 171 billion rand over the next five years.

INCA, which has a domestic long-term rating of AA- from European rating agency IBCA, will use funds raised by the bond issues to provide debt financing at low rates of interest to all infrastructure providers, ranging from local authorities, water utilities ad municipalities to private infrastructure companies.

Principal partners in INCA are First National Bank, the Commonwealth Development Corp and Southern Life, each with 20 percent. Other shareholders include Msele Ltd, Old Mutual and Women Investment Portfolio.
